newsitem.title: FRANCE: French steelmaker Usinor's '96 profits slide.
newsitem.headline: French steelmaker Usinor's '96 profits slide.

text.p: Usinor Sacilor SA, the big French steelmaker sold by the government last year, said Tuesday that 1996 profits tumbled, hurt by lower demand and weaker prices, forcing the company to cut its dividend.
Usinor Sacilor Chairman Francis Mer said he hoped that the steelmaker would improve earnings in 1997, helped by a rebound in demand.

"There should be a significant upturn in the second half of 1997 regarding earnings," he told a news conference, saying the first half of the year was looking disappointing. "We're hoping to do better in 1997."

The steelmaker said net profit slid to 1.49 billion francs ($259 million from a record 4.43 billion francs ($771 million) as sales fell to 71.1 billion francs ($12.4 billion) from 78.4 billion ($13.6 billion).
Usinor cut its dividend 25 percent but the reduction was smaller than some financial analysts had feared.

Operating profit fell 69 percent despite better financial results due to to lower debt and dividends from unconsolidated interests. The company managed to cut debt by nearly half to 6.5 billion francs ($1.1 billion) from 11.0 billion francs.
Sales of flat carbon steel fell 7.6 percent, sales of stainless steels and alloys declined 16.5 percent while speciality steels fell 9 percent.

Some 33.6 percent of sales were in France, 43.1 percent in other European countries and 23.3 percent in the rest of the world. The United States accounted for 11.8 percent of total sales. The geographic breakdown of sales was similar to 1995.
The company said demand was starting to rebound significantly in stainless and flat carbon products in Europe.
But it warned that while volumes were up, "average prices, at least for the first half, should be lower than those of 1996."
